authoredSolutions.26: The \(-NO_{2}\) group is strongly electron withdrawing through both \(-I\) and \(-R\) effects. It pulls electron density out of the ring, so the ring is deactivated towards electrophilic substitution: statement (B) is correct and (A) is wrong. The same withdrawal stabilises the negatively charged Meisenheimer intermediate formed when a nucleophile attacks the ring, particularly at the ortho and para positions, so the ring is activated towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution: statement (C) is correct and (D) is wrong. The correct statements are therefore (B) and (C).
authoredSolutions.27: Boiling points: HF boils at about 293 K, far above its neighbours, because of intermolecular hydrogen bonding; for the rest the boiling point rises with molar mass and dispersion forces, \(HCl\) 188 K, \(HBr\) 206 K, \(HI\) 238 K. The increasing order is therefore \(HCl < HBr < HI < HF\), so Statement I is true. Melting points: \(HCl\) 159 K, \(HBr\) 186 K, \(HF\) 190 K, \(HI\) 222 K. Hydrogen bonding lifts HF above HCl and HBr, but the much larger dispersion forces in HI still place it highest, giving \(HCl < HBr < HF < HI\), so Statement II is also true.
authoredSolutions.28: Metallic character decreases from left to right across a period and increases down a group. Valence shell configurations: \(P = [Ne]3s^{2}3p^{3}\) gives 5 valence electrons and \(F = [He]2s^{2}2p^{5}\) gives 7. The answer is therefore 5 and 7.

authoredSolutions.41: Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride. A primary amine gives an N-monosubstituted sulphonamide which still has an acidic N-H and therefore dissolves in alkali; a secondary amine gives an N,N-disubstituted sulphonamide with no N-H, which remains as an alkali insoluble solid; a tertiary amine does not react at all. From the list the secondary amines are N-methylaniline, N-methylmethanamine, N-propylaniline and N-phenylaniline (diphenylamine), which is four. Aniline, methanamine, phenylmethanamine, allylamine and isopropylamine are primary and give alkali soluble products, while N,N-dimethylmethanamine and N,N-dimethylaniline are tertiary and give no product. Hence the answer is 4.

authoredSolutions.72: The lift may stop only on floors \(4\) through \(10\), i.e. \(7\) floors. The three persons must exit on three different such floors, in \(7\times6\times5=210\) ways.
authoredSolutions.73: Differentiating the integral equation gives \(f'=2f+2x-3\) with \(f(0)=1\), which solves to \(f(x)=1-x\), so \(f(t)+2=3-t\). Then \(g'(x)=(3-x)^{15}(x-4)^6(x+12)^{17}\). The odd powers at \(x=3\) and \(x=-12\) give sign changes (the even power at \(4\) does not): \(g\) has a local maximum at \(q=3\) and a local minimum at \(p=-12\). Hence \(|p+q|=|-12+3|=9.\)
authoredSolutions.74: Let \(M=P+s(3,-1,0)\) lie on the line \((4,0,-1)+\mu(2,0,3)\). The \(y\)-coordinate gives \(\alpha=s\), and the distance \(|s|\sqrt{10}=13\sqrt{10}\Rightarrow|s|=13\). Matching the remaining coordinates gives \(\beta=\tfrac{115+9s}{2}\); the condition \(\beta<0\) forces \(s=-13\), so \(\alpha=-13,\;\beta=-1\). Thus \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=169+1=170.\)
authoredSolutions.75: \(A\) has trace \(2\) and det \(1\), so \((A-I)^2=0\) with \(N=A-I=\begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(A^{100}=(I+N)^{100}=I+100N\), so \(100B=100N\Rightarrow B=N\). Since \(N^2=0\), \(B^{100}=0\), and the sum of all elements of \(B^{100}\) is \(0.\)
